refuted.fact: F15: "Rack-level power claims NVIDIA made on the day: up to 40% more GPUs within the same site-power envelope and up to 35% higher token throughput"
refuted.why: The source puts those two bullets at FACTORY level, not rack level. The summit post reads 'At the factory level, NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS dynamically shifts power across racks as demand rises and falls. The payoff is significant: [40% / 35% bullets]'. Only the NEXT sentence is rack-level: 'Inside each rack, Intelligent Power Smoothing software and expanded energy buffering absorb short spikes'. Labelling the 40%/35% as rack-level puts the writer at the wrong level of abstraction.

additional_findings: NVIDIA'S OWN COMPANION POST IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT ABOUT THE SILICON VALLEY POWER EPISODE, and the researcher recorded both numbers without noticing the clash. The body states it twice as a 4 MW -> 3 MW drop ('power dropping from four megawatts to three, automatically'; 'power fell from four megawatts to three'), i.e. 25%. The 'Numbers at a glance' table states the same event as '40% | power demand reduction in under a minute | SVP automated response, Flexible Load Interconnect Program | Emerald AI / Future DSX Flex'. F24 carries the 4->3 MW figure, F29 carries the 40%, and the editorial_brief's suggested diagram uses '4 MW 降到 3 MW'. An article using both will contradict itself. The writer must pick one, say which part of the post it comes from, or state that NVIDIA describes the episode two different ways.

MISSING MATERIAL QUALIFIER IN F44: the DSX MaxLPS engineering blog's 125 kW->90 kW (GB200 NVL72) and 136 kW->101 kW (Vera Rubin NVL72) figures are NOT a like-for-like pair. The source says 'Vera Rubin NVL72 was tested with DeepSeek-R1, while GB200 NVL72 was tested with Kimi-K2.5'. The 39%/35% more racks and the ~1.5x vs 1.3-1.4x performance-per-watt therefore rest on different models. F44 omits this entirely.

MISSING MATERIAL QUALIFIER ON THE 1.6x MLPerf FIGURE: the summit post states it unqualified ('NVIDIA's MLPerf Inference v6.1 submissions delivered up to 1.6x higher performance than v6.0 through software optimizations alone'), but the dedicated MLPerf blog pins it to one platform and one model: 'In v6.1, GB300 NVL72 performance on Qwen3-VL improved up to 1.6x over v6.0 results.' If the article uses 1.6x, use the qualified version.

MISSING FROM F46: the MLPerf blog also states 'Nebius also submitted Vera Rubin NVL72 preview results and demonstrated excellent performance' - NVIDIA was not the only Vera Rubin submitter. The same blog independently characterises the SemiAnalysis AgentX 30x as achieved 'in preview testing', a stronger hedge than anything in the summit post and worth carrying into the how-to-read-vendor-numbers section.

PROVENANCE OF THE 15x FIGURE (F17): the summit post says 'roughly 15x the token volume of a simple chat request' with no attribution, but blogs.nvidia.com/blog/vera-rubin-nvl72-efficiency-ai-agents/ opens 'According to OpenRouter data, agentic AI workloads consume 15x more tokens than a simple chat request.' It is a third-party datapoint NVIDIA is relaying, not an NVIDIA measurement - the article should say so.
